steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Context refers to the social, cultural, political and historical circumstances in which a film is produced and received, and which shape its meaning and significance. | Key Fact: Social context includes the attitudes, values, structures and issues of the society in which a film is made — class relations, gender roles, racial dynamics and family structures. | Key Fact: Cultural context encompasses the shared beliefs, practices, traditions and media landscape that influence both filmmakers and audiences, including genre conventions and star images. | Key Fact: Political context involves the governmental systems, power structures, ideological debates and policy environments that affect what films are made and how they are received.
